=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (four leaves are clearly visible attached at the same node in a radial arrangement)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without leaflets)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (the leaf edges appear smooth without teeth)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (the leaves are elongated and widest near the base, tapering toward the tip)

    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the base of the leaf tapers gradually to the petiole)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with lateral veins branching off it)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, closely spaced, and numerous (forming a distinct pattern across the leaf surface)
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaf surface reflects light, indicating a smooth, glossy texture)

    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (the petioles are noticeably shorter than the leaf blades)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petioles appear rounded and cylindrical in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stem appears green, thin, and soft, characteristic of a young seedling)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem appears smooth without visible hairs)
    19.	Stem color: green (the stem is a vibrant green color)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears even and lacks ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (absent / present): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf nodes)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed

F. Notes: The seedling displays a distinct whorl of four leaves at the apex. The leaf venation is very prominent and reticulate, giving the surface a slightly textured appearance despite being shiny. The background shows a forest floor with leaf litter and other small plants.
